title: Dusting, damp wiping, washing and polishing furniture and surfaces
audience: Cleaners in any cleaning-group business who dust, damp wipe, wash and polish furniture, glazed items, telephones and office surfaces.
learningOutcomes: Fold and turn a duster so every part of the cloth is used and dirt is not spread.
Dust a surface from the edges inward, and dust the legs and sides from top to bottom.
Damp wipe or wash furniture with a cloth loaded with product, not with product sprayed onto the surface.
Apply polish to a dry surface using a cloth, and buff the treated areas to a high sheen.
Respect clear-desk limits by cleaning only clear areas and never moving or removing a client's papers.

instruction.heading: What these tasks have in common
instruction.body: Dusting, damp wiping, washing and polishing are the everyday surface tasks in most cleaning jobs. They look simple, which is why shortcuts creep in. The method is the same across all four: work from the edges inward, keep cloths clean, keep product off the air as far as possible, and finish with a surface that is clean, dry and free of smears. The source covers desks, furniture, glazed items, telephones and display furniture, and sets out the same care for each.

instruction.heading: Dusting
instruction.body: Fold the duster into thirds, then into thirds again, so that all of the face is used. Turn the cloth whenever it starts to clog. Dust the surface from the outside edges first, then the middle, using overlapping figure-of-eight passes. Dust the legs and sides from top to bottom, so that loosened dirt falls onto surfaces you have not yet cleaned. The aim is to remove dust, not to move it to the next surface.

instruction.heading: Desks, papers and glazed items
instruction.body: Clean only the clear areas of a desk. Do not move, remove, or read papers, and do not lift personal items to clean underneath them. Where a client runs a clear-desk routine, do not assume the desk is ready; ask the supervisor. Telephones are cleaned and sanitised as required, using a product approved for the surface. Glazed items, including framed pictures, mirrors, glazed noticeboards, display cases and bookcases, are cleaned using the glass method your business uses, and the cleaner must not allow product to run into the frame or onto the wall behind.

instruction.heading: Damp wiping, washing and polishing
instruction.body: Damp wiping and washing use a cloth loaded with diluted product. Do not spray the surface, because overspray reaches people and nearby items. Wipe the edges of the furniture first, then the middle, and do the legs and sides from bottom to top with product. Remove the product with a clean cloth and clean water, from the edges to the middle, and wipe the legs and sides from top to bottom. For polishing, the surface must be completely dry. Spray polish onto a clean duster rather than onto the surface, apply it to the outside edges first, then the middle, then the sides and legs, and buff all treated areas to a high sheen. Never sniff a duster to check whether it has polish on it.

instruction.heading: Blinds, curtains and care after use
instruction.body: Blinds and curtains are cleaned by the method that suits the material: washed where the material is washable, and aired or dry cleaned where appropriate. Where curtains are removed for cleaning at an approved premises, they must be replaced until they are returned. Curtain cleaning and blind-cleaning frequency are agreed with the client and recorded in the job system. After use, wash buckets, cloths and dusters thoroughly, hang the cloths to dry, store the bucket upside down, and keep the colour system.

procedure: Put on gloves. Check the surface is safe to clean, and confirm which papers and items must not be moved.
Fold the duster into thirds and then thirds again. Dust the edges first, then the middle, in figure-of-eight passes.
Dust the legs and sides from top to bottom, turning the cloth as it clogs.
For damp wiping, load the cloth with diluted product and wipe the edges first, then the middle. Treat the legs and sides from bottom to top.
Remove the product with a clean cloth and water, from the edges to the middle, and the legs and sides from top to bottom.
For polishing, confirm the surface is dry. Spray polish onto a clean duster, then apply to the edges, the middle, and the sides and legs.
Buff all polished areas to a high sheen, with no smears.
Wash all cloths and dusters, store the bucket upside down, and keep the colour groups separate.

workedExamples.situation: A client's wooden dining table is slightly damp from a spilled drink, and the client asks you to polish it now.
workedExamples.reasoning: Wait until the surface is completely dry before any polish is applied. Applying polish to a damp surface traps moisture and leaves marks. Dry the surface properly, then polish. Record the spill and any staining on the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A desk has a neat stack of papers in one corner, and you have been asked to dust the whole desk.
workedExamples.reasoning: Dust only the clear areas. Do not move or remove the papers. Record the area you could not clean and tell the supervisor, so the client can arrange for the desk to be cleared.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves, worn at all times when chemicals are used.
Eye protection when spraying polish or using diluted product close to the face.
Clean dusters and cloths, colour coded.
Plastic sheeting for the bucket area.
Disinfectant approved for telephones and similar surfaces.

commonErrors.error: Spraying product straight onto the surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Load the cloth, then wipe the surface.

commonErrors.error: Polishing a surface that is still damp.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the surface is completely dry before any polish is applied.

commonErrors.error: Sniffing a duster to see whether polish is on it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check by process and by sight. Never inhale a cloth to test it.

commonErrors.error: Moving a client's papers to clean underneath them.
commonErrors.prevention: Clean only the clear areas, and report any area you could not reach.

commonErrors.error: Dusting with a dirty cloth, which spreads dirt.
commonErrors.prevention: Fold, turn and change the cloth as it clogs.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Chemical use follows “Chemical competency: reading labels and safety data sheets”: check the SDS, dilute to the label, and do not mix products.
Overspray and inhalation: polish and product must not be sprayed near customers or their property. Ventilate where possible.
Telephones and other shared items: use a disinfectant approved for the surface and follow its label for contact time.
Privacy and property: papers and personal items are not read, moved or removed.

qualityStandard: Surfaces dusted from the outside edges inward, in figure-of-eight passes, with legs and sides dusted top to bottom.
No product sprayed directly onto a surface.
Polish applied to a dry surface and buffed to a high sheen with no smears.
No papers moved, and each uncleaned area recorded.
Mirrors and glazed items clean and free from smears.
documentationEvidence: Record of surfaces cleaned, and of any area not cleaned, with the reason.
Record of any damage, staining or fault found.
Blind or curtain schedule entry, where the task applies.
summary: Fold and turn the duster; dust from the edges inward.
Load the cloth with product; never spray the surface.
Polish only a dry surface, applied from a cloth and buffed to a sheen.
Clean only clear areas, and never move or read a client's papers.

knowledgeChecks.question: How should polish be applied to a dining table?
options: Sprayed directly onto the table until it is wet
Sprayed onto a clean duster and applied to a dry surface
Applied to a damp table so it spreads more easily

knowledgeChecks.question: A desk has papers on one corner. What should you do?
options: Move the papers aside carefully to clean underneath them
Read the papers to check whether they are important to the client
Clean only the clear areas, and do not move or remove the papers

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should you never sniff a duster to check whether polish is on it?
options: A strong smell shows the polish has cured, so a quick sniff confirms it
Inhaling polish and product is a hazard, so you check by process and by sight
Dusters do not hold polish, so the smell is misleading
